take_homes: A checker only means something if it doesn't move while the work is being scored, and you can prove that with a file hash.
A flat or green score may mean the checker is weak. Score a handful by hand against it once before trusting it.
Autonomy comes in grades (draft, review, automatic), and some categories always keep a human. I'd write that as an approval rule.

monday.move: Ask my controller to draft the month-end variance commentary with an agent. Then I'd write down three things a commentary must never get wrong (figures traceable to the ledger, named drivers, no unexplained plugs) as the first checker.
monday.when: Next month-end close, not this Monday
monday.stop_condition: If the checker passes something the controller would send back, or the monthly cost can't be stated, we stop.
monday.blocker: IT hasn't approved the tool for finance data, and nobody has told me the cost per month.

misconception.why: The checker, the standard and the approval levels are things my organisation writes and owns, not something in a licence. I still don't know what any of it costs, so I'm not convinced.

one_line: The best part was checking the checker, with a hash to prove it didn't move. Ninety minutes in and nobody had mentioned cost.
